Closeout_PolicyEffectDataContracts_Legac: Legs with the same natural target, the same mechanical metric and the same direction of change still occupy only one semantic leg even when they differ only in lifecycle arrangement (one-time, daily, immediate, ongoing or staged); a lifecycle difference is not a new mechanical metric and is carried by the Composite payload fields that can express that metric. Different natural targets, different mechanical metrics or different directions of change must still be split into separate semantic legs.

startupGoldCost and dailyMaintenanceGoldCost are policy funding metadata. Ordinary appropriations, budgets, funds, administrative spending, construction spending, startup fees and maintenance fees may only be reflected in these two policy cost fields; they must not produce duplicate execution legs or invented targets such as a treasury or fiscal account, and they do not prevent the benefit changes stated in the text from producing expressible effect legs. cost is non-executable policy spending; a real executable resource decrease must be written as source, not as cost. If a positive resource change stated in the text is funded only by policy funding such as startupGoldCost or dailyMaintenanceGoldCost and the text states no executable source, it must be written as an independent subject mechanism, not as a beneficiary with an omitted source; a linked mechanism with an omitted source is allowed only when the text really describes an external resource source that exists but is currently unknown. Real resource flows that the current Candidates can express, such as food transfers, tax transfers or personal account transfers, must keep both source and beneficiary/destination. If the mechanical target in the text belongs only to the exclusion range of all current Candidates or none of them can express it, effectIntents must be empty and must not be rewritten to another available target.

In a player local policy, soldier pay, salaries, allowances or local fiscal subsidies default to a positive character denar gain for the clan leader of the current owner of the affected settlement, unless the text explicitly names another individual recipient; the target description must keep the settlement binding and must not be generalized to all lords of the kingdom, soldiers or an unrelated issuer. Startup fees, maintenance fees and ordinary appropriations remain policy funding metadata only and must not produce duplicate negative character gold. This rule only fixes the target and direction of the local gold gain and does not limit which other effects the policy may have; other effects must be judged independently by the model from the full policy semantics, inputs, mechanisms and causality, and must not be added or excluded mechanically from a single keyword such as soldier pay or training. If gold, troop XP and other different mechanical metrics all hold, each must be kept separately.
